groundings.excerpt:
12: Abstract.
13: A minimal presentation of the cohomology ring of the flag manifold GL_{n}/B was given in [A. Borel, 1953]. This presentation was extended
14: by [E. Akyildiz–A. Lascoux–P. Pragacz, 1992] to a non-minimal one for all Schubert varieties. Work of [V. Gasharov–V. Reiner, 2002] gave a short, i.e. polynomial-size,
15: presentation for a subclass of Schubert varieties that includes the smooth ones. In [V. Reiner–A. Woo–A. Yong, 2011], a general shortening was found; it implies an exponential upper bound of 2^{n} on the number of generators required. That work states
16: a minimality
17: conjecture whose significance would be an exponential lower bound of \frac{\sqrt{2}^{n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}} on the number
18: of generators needed in worst case, giving the first obstructions to short presentations. We prove the minimality conjecture. Our proof uses the Hopf algebra structure of the ring of symmetric functions.

106: Then the basic ideal J_{v}, thought of as an ideal of H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}, is minimally generated by

109: That ( 4 ) generates J_{v} is [ 12 , Theorem 4.8] . The conjectural part, which we prove,
110: is the minimality claim, that is, no generator can be removed without changing the ideal.
